key_insight: This paper shows that Real-Bogus classifiers for time-domain astronomy can be trained without human labels by using injected transients and mostly bogus survey data. The result is an interpretable deep learning system that stays robust even when training data are heavily contaminated and can also report calibrated uncertainty.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of building reliable Real-Bogus classification models when expert labels are expensive, scarce, noisy, and survey-dependent, especially in the presence of strong class contamination.
method: Train a deep learning classifier without human-labeled examples by combining injected transients with bogus-dominated survey data.
Design the framework to remain robust under high levels of contamination in the training set.
Add uncertainty quantification so the model can indicate how confident it is in each prediction and support more trustworthy decisions.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a practical blueprint for label-free or weakly supervised classification in noisy real-world settings. It is especially valuable for scientific pipelines where interpretability, robustness, and calibrated confidence matter as much as accuracy.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing injected transients and bogus survey data feeding into the classifier
Two-class Real vs Bogus example panel with labeled prediction outputs
Uncertainty calibration plot or confidence histogram
Robustness chart showing performance under increasing class contamination
paper_title: Interpretable Human-Label-Free Deep Learning for Real-Bogus Classification with Uncertainty Quantification
paper_authors: Raphaël Bonnet-Guerrini, Bruno Sanchez, Dominique Fouchez, Benjamin Racine, Maya Guy
